mission: Engineer proteins that control the “operating system” of biology — starting with tools that improve blood-test performance, with longer-term aims in safer, more effective epigenetic medicines.

featured.description: Full-time wet-lab Research Associate role in San Carlos, CA ($70k–$95k + equity) supporting cell engineering, molecular biology, and assay work for Epinoma’s therapeutic/protein-engineering programs.
featured.responsibilities: Maintain cell lines/primary cells; perform transfection, transduction, and nucleofection; run basic imaging and flow cytometry; manage cell-line, plasmid, and bacterial stocks; clone genes/regulatory elements/vector components with QC; keep detailed experimental records and ELN entries; analyze technical data and improve routine methods; operate/maintain equipment and supplies; assist with SOP refinement. Senior RA track may independently design experiments and coordinate RA I tasks.
featured.qualifications: BS or MS in cellular biology or related field; new graduates with ≥6 months relevant lab experience welcome. Required skills: tissue culture; PCR, DNA binding, Western blot, ELISA, ChIP, immunostaining, multiplexed protein assays; cloning experience desirable; flow cytometry/imaging a plus; comfort with lab safety and biohazards. US citizen/visa only per posting. Senior RA: additional industry experience or project-design experience.

mission: Produce matched spatial transcriptomics, histopathology, and clinical datasets from real patient tumors for cancer therapeutics R&D and AI — so findings translate better in the clinic.

featured.description: Full-time computational biology role ($140k–$170k + equity; SF preferred / remote possible) owning Xenium post-run QC and secondary analysis of Origin’s spatial cancer datasets.
featured.responsibilities: Develop reproducible QC workflows for transcript detection, background, cell segmentation, transcript assignment, tissue/imaging artefacts, and run-to-run variation; align post-run H&E whole-slide images to Xenium DAPI and assess registration; work with pathologists to bring histological annotations into spatial data; analyze cell states, spatial neighbourhoods, tumour–immune interactions, and differential expression; use single-cell references where helpful.
featured.qualifications: PhD or postdoctoral research in spatial biology, or equivalent hands-on industry experience; Xenium or CosMx experience especially valuable (other spatial platforms welcome); oncology tissue / H&E WSI / multi-modality imaging experience preferred; strong Python or R and reproducible workflow skills. Prefer in-person San Francisco; remote possible for the right candidate.

mission: Help founders start companies through funding, intense advising, and a powerful alumni network — including bio/health startups ready to build full-time.

featured.description: Apply to a YC batch as a founder/co-founder. This is the specific batch application — not a job board listing at a portfolio company.
featured.responsibilities: If accepted: build and iterate the startup during the batch, talk to users, ship product, and present at Demo Day with your co-founders while working with YC partners.
featured.qualifications: A founding team (or strong solo case), a clear problem/solution thesis, and commitment to work on the company full-time if accepted. Bio/health startups are welcome when ready. Apply at the YC Apply page for the current batch cycle.

companyType: Deep-tech / biotech pre-seed accelerator and VC
mission: Fund and develop scientist-founders building deep-tech and biology-driven companies — with hands-on company-building support historically associated with IndieBio, now under SOSV NY and SOSV SF programs.

featured.description: Rolling application to SOSV startup development programs (including SOSV SF / SOSV NY biotech pathways formerly branded IndieBio). Selected teams enter diligence via screening calls and a short pitch.
featured.responsibilities: If accepted: execute a technical development plan during the program, iterate product/science with SOSV partners, and progress toward seed milestones with customized founder support.
featured.qualifications: A well-developed idea with technology worked out at least in principle and a strong team (typically ≥2 co-founders for funding; solo founders may apply but need a co-founder before funding). Programs may require in-person participation (clarify in interview). Apply via the SOSV application portal.

mission: Train researchers to test the commercial potential of deep science and engineering ideas through structured customer discovery — a pathway from lab research toward ventures and broader impact.

featured.description: NSF I-Corps pathway for academic teams to run intensive customer-discovery interviews and test value propositions for a research-based idea under an open Hub/Teams call.
featured.responsibilities: Complete customer-discovery interviews; test value propositions for a deep-tech or life-science concept; report learning with your I-Corps team (PI / entrepreneurial lead / mentor structure as defined by the call).
featured.qualifications: Typically an academic team with a deep-tech or life-science concept; eligibility depends on the specific Hub/Teams solicitation. Review current NSF I-Corps initiative guidance before applying.

mission: Help small businesses turn promising health technologies into products through SBIR/STTR research funding and commercialization support.

featured.description: Apply to current NIH SBIR/STTR funding opportunities via the SEED Find Funding page — this is a specific funding mechanism for qualifying small businesses, not a company careers board.
featured.responsibilities: Prepare and submit an NIH small-business research proposal under the open Omnibus or targeted solicitation; if awarded, execute the funded R&D plan and report progress under NIH terms.
featured.qualifications: A qualifying small business with a health-related innovation; PI and company eligibility rules are defined in the current Omnibus/solicitation. Review SEED’s SBIR/STTR funding opportunities page for open announcements and requirements.

mission: Support scientists and entrepreneurs building companies that cut greenhouse gas emissions, including bio-based approaches.

featured.position: Breakthrough Energy Fellows — Explorer / Innovator applicant
featured.description: Fellowship pathway for scientist-founders developing climate-critical technologies, including biological and industrial biotech solutions.
featured.responsibilities: Develop a venture thesis; engage technical and commercial milestones with program support; participate in cohort programming and mentorship.
featured.qualifications: Scientist or engineer founder (or founding team) with a climate-relevant technology; readiness for company formation. Confirm current track, deadlines, and eligibility on the Fellows page before applying.

mission: Help scientists and engineers turn research into startups through a funded fellowship with mentorship and community.

featured.description: Two-year fellowship supporting technical founders leaving academia/industry labs to build startups (including life-science hardware/biotech tools).
featured.responsibilities: Pursue full-time venture building; engage Activate programming, mentors, and milestones; develop customer discovery and fundraising readiness.
featured.qualifications: Technical founder background (PhD/postdoc/engineer common); commitment to building a company. Confirm cohort locations, stipend, and deadlines on Activate’s site.
